item.text: The existing post delay check reads `lastposttime` before creation; concurrent requests can all pass before that field is updated. The route already turns a thrown error into HTTP 400 with `status.code: "bad-request"`. I’m recording the guard’s needed scope and test coverage in the checkpoint.

/bin/bash -lc "cat > .codex-role-output/checkpoint.md <<'EOF'
Fault localization complete. POST /api/v3/topics is mounted in src/routes/write/topics.js and handled by Topics.create in src/controllers/write/topics.js. The controller directly awaits api.topics.create without a per-actor guard; the API then calls topics.post, which creates the entity and increments global/category counters. User.isReadyToPost in src/user/posts.js checks lastposttime but reads it before posts.create updates it, so concurrent requests can pass together. Route helper converts controller errors to HTTP 400; formatApiResponse gives status.code bad-request, while successful 200 gives status.code ok. Likely fix point: a synchronous per-uid/session lock acquisition in src/controllers/write/topics.js before first await, covering create and reply, with release in finally after all work. The lockPosting(req, error) interface should return posting<id> and throw the supplied error on collision. Existing API tests in test/api.js are schema and basic request tests; no concurrent burst assertion found. Validate one 200, remaining 400, one topic and matching counters. A process-local lock would not coordinate separate server processes; deployment scope remains uncertain.
EOF"

item.text:
The duplicate creation path is in [topics.js](/app/src/controllers/write/topics.js:19): each request enters `api.topics.create` without a per-user guard. The post delay check in [user/posts.js](/app/src/user/posts.js:8) can read the same `lastposttime` for overlapping requests, allowing each to reach topic creation and increment the counters.

The likely fix is a lock acquired before the controller’s first `await`, keyed by authenticated `uid` or guest `sessionID`, and released in `finally`. A collision should throw the supplied error. The route already converts controller errors to HTTP 400 with `status.code: "bad-request"`; a successful 200 has `status.code: "ok"`. The lock’s behavior across multiple server processes remains uncertain.

I recorded the findings in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). Project source and tests were not changed because this run’s specialist instructions limit it to fault localization.
